A + B · Rail that opens
  • Closed, it's A: the hairline, a dot and the year for each chapter, the current one's name, and "Play the story" above.
  • Hover over it and it opens like B: a soft shade comes in from the left, the rows spread out, and every chapter's name shows large beside its year (the current year in amber). Move away and it folds back. It waits a beat before opening, so a pointer passing by doesn't open it.
  • Closed, it stays as quiet as the top bar; open, the shade makes it readable on any scene. On a phone, tap it: it opens across the screen, and picking a chapter closes it.
All three would work like this
  • Clicking a chapter cuts there with a quick fade, onto its title card, instead of scrolling through everything before it.
  • Play scrolls the page by itself at a steady pace, waiting a few seconds on each card, with the music following. Any scroll, swipe or key gives you control again (it pauses).
  • This mock-up has two stills per chapter, and a chapter plays in about 5 seconds. On the page it'd be the real scenes moving.

Try it: Play, click a chapter, scroll to pause. Space plays or pauses; the arrow keys step through.
